purpose.title: What are we testing?
lines: 1. Is the Bose–Hubbard ED construction correct?
2. Can basic NQS reproduce its ground state with supervision?
3. Does stochastic VMC work on small, checkable systems?
4. What does a fixed-N fit predict in untrained sectors?
purpose.footer: Building and benchmarking a physics tool. Architecture searches and optimizer rankings are separate research directions.

criticality.title: Criticality and finite-size validation
lines: $\Delta_N=E_1(N)-E_0(N),\qquad F_{\rm abs}=|\langle\Psi_0|\Psi_\theta\rangle|$
$E_\theta-E_0\geq\Delta_N(1-F_{\rm abs}^2)$
A closing gap weakens energy as a certificate of fidelity.
Gaplessness does not imply that variational Monte Carlo must fail.
Finite tori require their own checks before bulk claims.
criticality.footer: Bound assumes a unique ground state and a normalized trial state in the same sector. Use total expectation energy, not energy density or one noisy MC estimate. Carleo & Troyer, Science355,602(2017), demonstrate finite-size NQS-VMC at criticality; no thermodynamic guarantee follows.

raw_projected.title: Raw network and physical state
lines: $\widetilde{\Psi}_\theta(\mathbf{n})=e^{f_\theta(\mathbf{n})},\qquad N(\mathbf{n})=\sum_i n_i$
$Z_N=\sum_{N(\mathbf{n})=N}e^{2f_\theta(\mathbf{n})}$
$\Psi_{\theta,N_0}(\mathbf{n})=\delta_{N(\mathbf{n}),N_0}\,e^{f_\theta(\mathbf{n})}/\sqrt{Z_{N_0}}$
The target fixed-N state is zero outside its sector.
Finite exp(f) is strictly positive, including untrained sectors.
raw_projected.footer: The canonical VMC sampler implements the projected distribution. Here mu=0 is a fixed-sector energy convention; it does not assert that N0 is the grand-canonical ground-state sector.

leakage_definition.title: How do we define leakage?
lines: $P_{\rm full}(N)=Z_N/\sum_{K=0}^{N_{\max}N_s}Z_K,\qquad \ell_{\rm full}=1-P_{\rm full}(N_0)$
$W=\{N_0-2,\ldots,N_0+2\},\qquad P_W(N)=Z_N/\sum_{K\in W}Z_K$
$\ell_{\rm near}=\sum_{N\in W,\ N\ne N_0}P_{\rm full}(N)$
$R_N=Z_N/Z_{N_0},\qquad \overline{w}_N=Z_N/d_N$
$F_{\rm full}=\sqrt{P_{\rm full}(N_0)}\,F_{N_0}$
leakage_definition.footer: Ns=LxLy=9. Full means the stated truncated local basis0..Nmax, not unbounded Fock space. PW is window-conditional, not global. dN counts configurations. Ffull compares the raw full-space state to the zero-embedded canonical ED vector; overlaps are absolute and unsquared.

nonidentifiability.title: Fixed-sector data cannot fix leakage
lines: $f'_\theta(\mathbf{n})=f_\theta(\mathbf{n})+h(N),\qquad h(N_0)=0$
$Z'_N=e^{2h(N)}Z_N,\qquad \Psi'_{\theta,N_0}=\Psi_{\theta,N_0}$
All canonical fits and observables stay unchanged.
RBM visible biases implement a number tilt within the same family.
Neighboring-sector weights depend on an untrained extension.
nonidentifiability.footer: This is an exact postprocessing control, not a claim that each finite neural architecture realizes every h. Examples: h=a(N−N0) tilts sectors; h=−lambda(N−N0)^2 suppresses both sides. Distinct projected particle-number states are orthogonal; these weights are not transition probabilities.

projection.title: Projection is an exact control
lines: $\Psi^{\rm projected}_\theta\propto P_{N_0}\widetilde{\Psi}_\theta$
$\ell^{\rm projected}_{\rm full}=0,\qquad F^{\rm projected}=F_{N_0}$
No retraining is needed; canonical predictions are preserved.
A number penalty on fixed-N training samples is identically zero.
projection.footer: Restricting sampled configurations is standard for U(1) conservation in canonical VMC (Pei & Clark2024). Learning an off-sector penalty requires off-sector examples or sampling; explicit output masks can instead impose it directly. Raw leakage is an extension diagnostic, not an error of projected VMC or proof of wasted capacity.
